methodological_questions: Measurement of defensive impact on opponent performance
Statistical reliability and stability of team-level metrics
Confounding factors for half-to-half performance changes
Appropriate sample size for establishing team traits
Separating defensive adjustments from offensive execution
Controlling for regression to the mean

historical_evidence.finding: Defensive scheme change within game and across games (inferred labels) was untestable, with inferred label unable to separate real defensive adjustment from offense executing differently; near-uniform transition matrices consistent with label noise.

Adapt vs continue matched-pair overall-offense excess was untestable. Group B caliper-0.10 CI includes 0 (p=0.386, n=255 clusters=242); Group B is a reconstructed post-hoc cohort, not a validated successful-adaptation sample.

Opponent-relative leverage prevalence sweep found exploit available 33.3%; trap 23.3%; both 6.7%; neither 50.0%; median best edge 3.79%. Edges depend only on the defense (e.g. DAL PNR +9.2% for every offense), so they are not matchup-specific.
Player BEST/AVOID tier tendency in H2 trigger games (55 series) showed Team AVOID% ranges 50.6% (ORL) to 6.8% (SAC); team BEST% 0.0%-15.8%.
Structural concentration vs defensive vulnerability was rejected. C1a rho=+0.079 p=0.0882 CI[-0.114,+0.234]; C1b rho=+0.095 p=0.0738; robust 0.2/0.3 also fail.

Persistent Impact Score Level 1 gate was an artifact. FAIL decay-sanity: DRIVE lifts +0.015,+0.020,+0.018,+0.021,+0.020 (flat). Within-team: DRIVE lag-1 +0.015 to -0.002. Flat non-decaying lifts collapse under within-team baseline; team-quality confound.
Coverage feasibility gate was supported. G1 72 team-seasons with >=200 poss in both; G2 |rho(COVERED,TALENT)|=0.042, aux R2=0.203; G3 rho(TALENT,PPP)=+0.027.
Double-suppression stacking (POST_UP then PUTBACK) was inconclusive. Stacked delta -0.071 vs additive prediction -0.232 (less t).

H1 usage as predictor of H2 suppression (distribution shift) was rejected. Test B: all BH-adjusted null/WEAK (PNR ATT=+0.0313 BH_p=0.0658 WEAK; others NULL). Predictive lift over mean reversion is only +0.039 (0.550 vs 0.511). Bulk of H2 suppression is RTM.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attempt to measure defensive scheme change using inferred labels
failed_approaches.why: A_unanswerable (question not answerable with the data or design); LABEL_ERROR: inferred label cannot separate real defensive adjustment from offense executing differently.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Measuring the effect of abandoning a suppressed play type on H1->H2 decline
failed_approaches.why: A_unanswerable (question not answerable with the data or design); PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER: Group B caliper-0.10 CI includes 0; Group B is a reconstructed post-hoc cohort, not a validated successful-adaptation sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing if structural concentration predicts defensive vulnerability
failed_approaches.why: B_powered_null (adequately powered null result); low_power_large_MDE and small_sample: not underpowered (30 franchises) but CI spans 0.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Measuring decaying cross-possession memory of play-type actions
failed_approaches.why: C_artifact (apparent effect produced by a construction, selection or labelling flaw); confounding: Flat non-decaying lifts collapse under within-team baseline; team-quality confound.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Measuring additive effects of double-suppression stacking
Using H1 usage to predict H2 suppression after controlling for H1 PPP / mean reversion
failed_approaches.why: B_powered_null (adequately powered null result); selection_or_regression_to_the_mean (RTM_SELECTION): Matched ATT does not survive BH; predictive lift over mean reversion is only +0.039 (0.550 vs 0.511). Bulk of H2 suppression is RTM.

evidence_establishes: The bulk of observed H2 suppression (H2-H1 change in opponent performance) is attributable to regression to the mean (FAM:SF-APPS-070), not a predictive effect from H1 usage.

It is difficult to reliably measure defensive effects on opponent performance, as attributing observed changes solely to defense is challenging due to label noise and confounding factors like team quality (FAM:SF-APPA-005, FAM:SF-CHT-029).

Some defensive characteristics (e.g., coverage, defensive 'edges') can exist as team-level traits independent of specific matchups (FAM:SF-PAP-009, FAM:SF-APPA-034), but not all hypothesized defensive vulnerabilities are reliable (FAM:SF-PAP-024).
Small sample sizes and issues with cohort definition can lead to untestable conclusions when studying within-game performance changes (FAM:SF-APPS-025).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether *any* portion of H2-H1 change can be reliably attributed to a specific, consistent defensive team trait, beyond regression to the mean.
Specific methodologies for isolating a defensive 'effect' on H2-H1 change from other factors, given the strong influence of regression to the mean.
The specific magnitude or nature of reliable defensive team traits that *could* influence H2-H1 changes, if such an influence exists.
own_inferences: If the majority of H2-H1 change is regression to the mean, then the signal-to-noise ratio for any underlying defensive 'effect' is likely very low, making it extremely difficult to identify and measure reliably as a team trait.
The term 'reliable team trait' implies consistency and predictability. If the primary driver is RTM, then the 'effect' is not a stable trait but a statistical artifact of initial performance.
uncertainties: The exact proportion of H2-H1 change that is *not* due to regression to the mean, and whether that residual can be explained by defensive traits.
How to define and measure 'defense's effect' on H2-H1 change in a way that is robust to confounding factors and regression to the mean.

historical_effect.explanation: The historical evidence, particularly FAM:SF-APPS-070, fundamentally changed the understanding of H2-H1 performance changes. It established that the bulk of H2 suppression is due to regression to the mean, making it highly improbable that a 'defense's effect' on this change is a reliable team trait. This finding shifts the assessment from 'difficult but possible' to 'highly unlikely to find a meaningful signal'.

blocking_constraints.text: The primary driver of H2-H1 change in opponent performance has been established to be regression to the mean (FAM:SF-APPS-070). This makes isolating a distinct 'defense's effect' extremely difficult, as the signal will be heavily obscured by this statistical phenomenon.

Prior work has shown that analyses of sequential effects are prone to confounding by factors like team quality (FAM:SF-CHT-029). Without robust controls, any observed H2-H1 changes could be attributed to overall team strength rather than a specific defensive trait.

Attributing observed changes in opponent performance solely to 'a defense's effect' is challenging, as it's difficult to separate true defensive adjustments from changes in offensive execution or other game flow factors (FAM:SF-APPA-005).

Establishing reliable team traits and subtle effects often requires large sample sizes. While 120 team-seasons are available, the effect size for a 'defense's effect' beyond RTM is likely very small, requiring significantly more data or a very precise measurement to achieve useful power (FAM:SF-APPS-025, FAM:SF09).

prior_work.summary: Previous research (FAM:SF-APPS-070) has already shown that H2 suppression, which is a key component of 'H2-H1 change', is predominantly explained by regression to the mean. This directly addresses the underlying mechanism of the proposed phenomenon, indicating that a distinct 'defense's effect' beyond RTM is unlikely to be a significant or reliable factor. Other studies highlight general difficulties in measuring defensive impact and isolating effects from confounders.

risks.text: The most significant risk is that any observed 'effect' will largely be regression to the mean, making it difficult to demonstrate a distinct defensive trait. This has been explicitly shown in FAM:SF-APPS-070.

Team quality, opponent strength, game context (e.g., score margin, home/away), and offensive adjustments are strong confounders that could explain H2-H1 changes, rather than a specific defensive trait. FAM:SF-CHT-029 highlighted team-quality confound.

Defining and reliably measuring 'a defense's effect' on opponent H2-H1 change is inherently difficult. Distinguishing it from offensive adjustments or random variance is a major challenge, as indicated by FAM:SF-APPA-005.

Given the likely small effect size of any true defensive trait beyond RTM, 120 team-seasons might be insufficient to detect such a subtle effect with adequate statistical power (FAM:SF-APPS-025, FAM:SF09).
If exploring various ways to define 'defense's effect' or 'H2-H1 change', there's a risk of false positives from multiple comparisons.

design.estimand: The residual variation in opponent's H2-H1 change in points per possession (PPP) after controlling for opponent's H1 PPP and other game-level confounders, attributable to a specific defensive team trait.
design.sample: NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26 regular seasons and playoffs. Total 120 team-seasons, implying approximately 2400-3000 team-games (assuming 30 teams * 4 seasons * ~20 games/season for team-game unit, or 30 teams * 4 seasons for team-season unit).
design.power: Not achievable at useful levels given the dominance of RTM. A minimum detectable effect size for a 'reliable team trait' would need to be very large to overcome the noise.
design.controls: Control for opponent's H1 PPP (to account for regression to the mean), opponent team quality, defensive team quality, game pace, score differential at half-time, home/away advantage, and opponent's offensive play-type distribution in H1. This would require a sophisticated mixed-effects model or propensity score matching.
design.falsification: A falsification test would involve demonstrating that the hypothesized defensive 'effect' is robust to different specifications of the RTM control, and that it does not collapse under within-team baselines (as seen in FAM:SF-CHT-029).
design.multiplicity: Given the decision not to proceed, multiplicity is not a concern. If proceeding, a strict correction like Benjamini-Hochberg for a pre-registered set of defensive traits would be necessary.
design.decision_rule: Reject the null hypothesis if the estimated coefficient for the defensive trait is statistically significant (p < 0.05) and robust across sensitivity analyses, and the effect size is practically meaningful (e.g., > 0.05 PPP change), after accounting for RTM and confounders. However, based on prior evidence, this is highly unlikely.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26 regular season and playoffs play-by-play, substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary, and derived play-type possession records.

Confounding factors for half-to-half performance changes
Appropriate sample size for establishing team traits

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

- testability.p_testable: probability that the question can be answered with the stated data at useful statistical power.
- prior_work.already_answered: whether retrieved earlier work already answered substantially the same question.

- predicted_outcome: probabilities (summing to 1) of what a competent test of the question as posed would conclude:

- decision: proceed, proceed_with_changes (state the changes in design), or do_not_proceed.
- design: a pre-registration-quality plan even if the decision is do_not_proceed (then describe the minimum viable test).
